edges.description: Loss of Gibbin in human embryonic stem cell-derived organoids disrupts mesodermal gene expression. The study used engineered Gibbin-mutant cells and chimeric mice, so it shows the consequence of losing Gibbin rather than of a specific heterozygous patient allele.

De novo AHDC1 truncation is associated with structural brain anomalies and a neurodevelopmental phenotype, but no molecular or cellular step between the variant and abnormal brain development has been demonstrated.
Upper airway abnormalities are recurrent in XGS; how AHDC1 variants produce them is unknown.
Chimeric Gibbin mouse mutants show craniofacial patterning defects that the authors relate to patient phenotypes; the link to human facial features is by analogy.
Corpus callosum hypoplasia is a structural manifestation of the disrupted brain development.
Posterior fossa cysts are a second recurrent structural finding.
Intellectual disability is a core consequence of the disordered neurodevelopment.
Global developmental delay reflects the disordered neurodevelopment.
Delayed motor milestones are among the earliest manifestations.
Speech delay, especially of expressive language, is a core neurodevelopmental feature.
Congenital hypotonia is attributed to the central neurodevelopmental disorder; no myopathic basis has been reported.
Seizures occur in a minority and are a manifestation of central nervous system involvement.
Ataxia and other movement disorders often become apparent in childhood or adolescence.
Autism spectrum features are part of the neurodevelopmental phenotype.
Structural narrowing or collapse of the upper airway is the proposed cause of obstructive sleep apnea in XGS.
Laryngomalacia is one of the upper airway abnormalities reported.
Reproduces developmental patterning defects attributed to loss of Gibbin mesodermal function.
edges.limitations: Chimeric mosaic mutants rather than germline heterozygotes carrying a patient truncation; neurodevelopmental and sleep phenotypes were not the focus of the study.

nodes.description: A heterozygous, usually de novo, nonsense or frameshift variant in the single coding exon of AHDC1. Because the variant lies in the last (only) coding exon, the mutant transcript is predicted to escape nonsense-mediated decay and could encode a truncated protein lacking the AT-hook DNA-binding motifs and conserved regions downstream of the truncation. Escape from nonsense-mediated decay has been confirmed in one patient's sample. Whether the variant acts through loss of function or a dominant-negative effect has not been established.

nodes.description: Wild-type AHDC1 is nuclear. Truncated forms modelled on patient alleles show either a diffuse distribution (short N-terminal fragments) or aggregation in the nucleolus (mid-protein truncations). This was observed on transient overexpression in cell lines, so whether endogenous truncated protein is produced and mislocalized in patient neural cells is not known.

nodes.description: Gibbin binds enhancers and promoters together with many zinc-finger transcription factors and methyl-CpG-binding proteins. Its loss increases DNA methylation at GATA3-dependent mesodermal genes, impairs dermal maturation in skin organoids and, in chimeric mouse mutants, produces craniofacial, abdominal wall and epidermal patterning defects. The study proposes that some XGS features arise from abnormal mesoderm maturation; how far this explains the neurodevelopmental phenotype has not been tested.
